answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making identity expensive and auditable. Each agent holds a hardware-attested credential from a secure enclave, one per device, plus a stake slashed if duplicated. To field a thousand fake voters, an attacker must rent a thousand machines and post a thousand bonds, so cost climbs linearly while reward stays flat. The registry keeps an immutable echo of every device key, exposing any key that enrolls twice. Colocated farms cannot cheat: whether servers sit in a juniper cabinet or on a basalt slab, each identity needs its own enclave and stake.
